cues.zh: 混水龙头，了不起的发明，却似乎被英国错过了。
cues.en: The mixer tap, brilliant invention, and yet something that seems to have passed Britain by.

cues.zh: 美国人过来会问，为什么我们的水龙头看起来像1940年代的。
cues.en: You'll get Americans coming over here and asking why our taps look like they're from the 1940's.

cues.zh: 甚至在这里，我父母的浴室里——我这周末来看望他们，他们
cues.en: And even here, in my parents' bathroom -- I'm visiting my folks this weekend and they

cues.zh: 刚装了一间新浴室——还是冷热水分开的两个龙头。
cues.en: just had a new bathroom put in -- separate hot and cold taps.

cues.zh: 关于原因有各种理论，大多围绕着
cues.en: And there are all sorts of theories about why that might be, generally revolving

cues.zh: “因为我们是英国人”“坚忍克己”“你知道我们不需要混水龙头，我们从来就没有过”。
cues.en: around 'Well we're British,' and 'Stiff upper lip,' and 'You know we don't need mixer taps. We've never had them.'

cues.zh: 这有一定道理，但也要追溯到二战后英国房屋的建造方式。
cues.en: And well, that's partly true, but it also goes back to how houses in Britain were constructed after World War II.

cues.zh: 在英国大多数老房子里，阁楼上有一个冷水储水箱。尺寸还算合理，大约250升，
cues.en: In most old British houses there's a cold water storage tank up in the attic. It's reasonably sized, about 250 liters,

cues.zh: 它再供给一个热水储水箱，用于中央供暖，
cues.en: and that in turn feeds a hot water storage tank that's for the central heating,

cues.zh: 以及浴室、厨房等的热水，等等。
cues.en: and for hot water in the bathroom, and in the kitchen, and so on.

cues.zh: 但问题是，那未必是完全安全的饮用水。因为那个冷水储水箱，
cues.en: But the trouble is that might not be entirely safe drinking water. Because that cold water storage tank,

cues.zh: 在一些维护不当的房子里，可能敞露在外，或者淤积了泥沙，或者覆满了
cues.en: in some houses that weren't properly maintained, might have been open to the elements, or silted up, or covered

cues.zh: 铁锈，或者，在一个你可以读到的特别案例里，里面还漂着几只死老鼠。
cues.en: with iron rust, or, in one particular case you can read about, have a couple of dead rats floating in it.

cues.zh: 那种水从技术上讲可能不能喝。而根据规定——我查过规定——
cues.en: That water might technically not be drinkable. And under the regulations - I looked up the regulations -

cues.zh: 它不算作饮用水。而冷水呢，至少在厨房里，有时在
cues.en: it is not counted as drinking water. The cold, meanwhile, at least certainly in the kitchen, and sometimes the

cues.zh: 浴室里也是，冷水直接来自市政供水。那才算可饮用。
cues.en: bathroom, too, the cold water comes straight from the mains. That counts as drinkable.

cues.zh: 所以问题就在这儿：你有冷的、安全的、规定称之为“卫生”的饮用水，而你还有，
cues.en: So here's the thing: You have cold, safe, the regulations call it 'wholesome', drinking water, and you have,

cues.zh: 嗯，几乎肯定安全但从技术上、从法规上不算的，热水。
cues.en: well, almost certainly safe but not technically, not legally under the regulations, hot water.

cues.zh: 两者永不相交。如果你装了混水龙头，那么从技术上讲，在最坏的情况下，那些不卫生的热水——
cues.en: And never the twain shall meet. If you have a mixer tap, then technically, the unsafe hot water, in the worst case

cues.zh: 比如当回流阀失效、主供水关闭时，那些不卫生的水可能会倒流回去，
cues.en: scenario, when there is a backwash valve failure and the mains turns off, that unsafe water could go back,

cues.zh: 回流穿过整个系统，流到外面，污染整条街或整个
cues.en: backwash through all the systems, and go out to contaminate the rest of the street or the rest of the

cues.zh: 供水系统。这是不合法的，所以不能装混水龙头。不能让水流交叉。当然，如今
cues.en: water system. That's not legal, therefor no mixer tap. You don't cross the streams. Nowadays, of course,

cues.zh: 情况有些不同了。这栋房子的热水储水箱几个月前被拆掉了。阁楼现在又变成了一个
cues.en: it's a little bit different. This house had its hot water tank ripped out a few months ago. The attic is now just a big

cues.zh: 空荡荡的大空间。而楼下有一项非常现代、闪亮的技术，可以按需加热水。
cues.en: empty space again. And, well, there is a very modern, shiny bit of technology downstairs that heats up water

cues.zh: 所有新建房屋都走这条路。如果它们装了混水龙头，那完全没问题。但是……
cues.en: on demand. All new built houses go this way. If they've got mixer taps, it'll be absolutely fine. But...

cues.zh: 我记得小时候有人告诉我“千万别喝热水龙头的水”。这句话我一直记着。即使是现在，如果有那种冷热混合水龙头
cues.en: I remember being told as a kid 'never drink from the hot water tap.' And that stuck with me. Even now, if there is a mixer tap

cues.zh: 我想接水喝，我会先放几秒冷水，确保任何不安全的物质
cues.en: and I want to drink from it, I will run the cold water for a few seconds just to make sure anything that's unsafe

cues.zh: 都被冲出来了。即使是现在，旧习惯难改。而且有时候，这些做法就是让人觉得更安全一点。
cues.en: has come out of it. Even now old habits die hard. And sometimes these things just feel a bit safer.
